activation.note: Activation concerns planning/decomposition and implementation-flavored inputs to that activity. Non-user-facing internal objectives are covered by the source's positive requirement for user-facing jobs, not merely its prohibition on technology choices. ADR/test authoring and subsequent coding are outside that obligation. Semantic classification is honestly labeled llm_judged, and phase detection explicitly requires a new observer; artifact and task-text facts describe directly inspectable signals rather than claiming semantic certainty.

audit.summary: All ten segments survive at their claimed destinations, including both alternatives for handling implementation decisions and the original example. The added ordering advice is explicitly declared, there are no waivers or shared-node relocations, and then states one user-facing decomposition obligation.

segmentChecks.note: The then clause requires every plan item to state a user-facing job rather than how the system is built; why and avoid[0] reinforce the same distinction.
prefer[0] and prefer[1] retain both reframing and routing to tests/ADRs, including the Redis-to-catalog example; avoid[1] and evidence[1] preserve the obligation's scope.
The domain_capability term name is retained verbatim in verifier_detail[0] and then.
The definition 'a user-facing job the system performs' is retained in verifier_detail[0] and operationally stated in then.
The technology_choice term name is retained in verifier_detail[1] and prefer[1].
verifier_detail[1] preserves the implementation-decision definition and both permitted dispositions, which also appear in prefer and why.

unobservable: phase: explicitly needs a new observer to determine that the agent is planning or decomposing work.
finding: requires LLM semantic judgement about whether an item is a user-facing job or is implementation-flavored, so a Datalog engine cannot directly observe it.

review.summary: All six knowledge-bearing segments are preserved, including the complete example, both handling alternatives, and both term definitions. The coder-facing guidance clearly tells a planner to produce user-facing jobs and either reframe or route implementation decisions. Activation is not fully deterministic because phase needs a new observer and finding is LLM-judged, but these limitations are accurately disclosed and do not undermine the auditor's PASS.
